title: devlab mcp: the phone for any agent
note: devlab mcp (rmcp 3.10, stdio): run, put, get, health_report, health_run, kernel_install, kernel_try, kernel_status, reboot - each the function the command line calls; nothing but the protocol on standard output (what the functions said is returned, their talk goes to standard error). Proven 2026-11-17 against surya by a raw MCP exchange: initialize, the 9 tools listed, health_report with the phone's own verdict, kernel_status, run as root.

title: Flashing
note: devlab flash did its first real flash (2026-11-10): the pristine stock image, the manifest's fixes baked in, the device tree fingerprinted (a43d069d0a49adcd), the phone back with all 20 checks passing.

title: A known gap counted apart from a failure, when a run is filed
note: devlab gather files each run test_runs row with gaps: failures in the manifest [health] gaps, counted apart from failed, as the phone own verdict counts them (docs gaps-on-the-face). Columns are named in the insert, so the table order may change without a filing breaking. Proven 2026-11-17 by filing run 20261117-013421 again into a copy of docs: 25 pass, 4 failed, 5 in gaps, 1 skipped - as the backfill counted it.

title: Gathered once the phone is quiet, landed again if main moved
note: Measured 2026-11-17 (conveyor session): in about 2 h the watch gathered 5 times and 2 landings failed, other sessions having landed in docs and surya-lab meanwhile; each boot cost two PRs, two CI rounds and a Pages build. Now the board hears the verdict at once, but gathering waits until the phone has gone 15 minutes without a new boot (a run of kernel tries is one landing per place), and a landing that does not go through closes its own PR and branch and is tried again from main as it then is, 3 times in all; what is still unfiled is filed in the next quiet period.

title: A turn does not end with unlanded changes
note: A Stop hook (devlab guard stop) that refuses to end a turn while a place the session worked in holds changes not landed: the places are read off the transcript (the cwd of its Bash calls and the files it edited), each checked with git status and its branch against origin/main. Waits on: telling what the session worked in from the hook input alone, cheaply.

title: The ways, held for agents: devlab guard
note: Claude Code hooks on the lab call devlab guard: PreToolUse refuses git push to main, python/pip, and ssh/scp/sftp/rsync/sshpass to a phone address devlab has met (each manifest leaves its addresses in the state); SessionStart prints lab-agent guide and the inbox. Proven by replaying each event to the built binary (refused with exit 2 and the reason; a branch push, ls, grep python allowed) and by unit tests of each shape (sudo, env, timeout, xargs, sh -c, $(...), lab-agent root-exec).

title: Health, after every boot
note: devlab test, health, watch: regressions raise one board task.

title: Every change ends with the health report
note: Every change devlab makes ends with the phone's health: phone reboot and kernel try wait for the report the new boot writes by itself (the test kernel's boot is measured like any other), provision runs the suite at once; the verdict is said, the report brought to the lab's tests/results, and the command fails when the phone is unhealthy. Proven 2026-11-17 by a reboot of surya: back, then healthy (29 pass, 4 in known gaps) and the report brought, 3 minutes in all. kernel try uses the same step and is not yet proven live. A change made by hand through phone sh/root has no step to end: devlab suite run, or the MCP door's health tool.

title: devlab-health as an Alpine package
note: Through the package conveyor once cv-apk publishes Alpine repositories; until then devlab puts the files on the phone.  Read 2026-11-17 (orchestration): held by three things not yet there - lab-tools cuts no releases (no tags, no release flow); the conveyor cv-apk is open and unbegun (publish.yml builds and signs pacman only); and an Alpine repository needs its own RSA signing key (abuild-keygen), kept as a secret of lab-tools, its public half committed and baked into the phone. Path: (1) the key, on the author word; (2) cv-apk in the conveyor: build the APKBUILD in an aarch64 Alpine container (an arm64 runner), abuild-sign the index, publish under the pages site alpine/aarch64, verify every signature, install it in a postmarketOS container; (3) lab-tools: release-plz, health/APKBUILD (devlab-health, the checks, lib.sh, the service and timer), packaging/conveyor.toml; (4) devlab provision adds the repository and its key, and suite put gives way to the package.

title: The checks surya-lab ran from the lab, carried into the suite
note: surya-lab tests/automatic/checks.sh retired on 2026-11-17 (its decision 2026-11-17-the-lab-s-own-conveyor-retires); four of its checks are not yet in the phone suite: bt-sees-devices (a 6 s bluetoothctl scan; skip when none answers - generic, 70-bluetooth.sh), modem-ready for modem-calls and modem-sms as well as modem-data (the modem state once a SIM is in - generic, 60-modem.sh), the audio DSP crashes that came with a suspend counted apart (awk between PM: suspend entry and 2 s after exit - generic, 30-processors.sh), and speaker-stereo (the HiFi__Speaker sink is 2ch - surya own, tests/health, bring-up). The retired file is in surya-lab history before that decision.

title: Gathering is one command
note: devlab gather now: the phone's reports into the device lab's tests/results, every unfiled run into docs' test_results and test_runs. Proven 2026-11-17: 5 reports brought from surya, 9 runs filed (5 from 2026-11-10 never filed by hand; one run spoiled by a check of mine that could not write was taken out everywhere). Next: a device lab keeps its runs as its own data once the language gives a test run a shared shape (ocoeco sign a-test-run-has-no-shared-shape).

title: The phone checks its own health after every boot
note: devlab-health (static Rust runner, health/) and the generic checks: storage, kernel (oops, new warnings, processor crashes, failed units), signal processors, sound cards, Wi-Fi, modem, Bluetooth, display and input, the other parts, then the shell's sound output; a phone's own checks and expectations from its manifest ([health]); known gaps measured but not ill health. Proven on surya 2026-11-17: put by devlab suite put now, the phone ran it by itself 120 s after a reboot and said healthy: 29 pass, 4 in known gaps, 1 not measured, 0 fail.

title: One controlled suspend and wake in the suite
note: An RTC wake alarm suspend, as postmarketos-test-suspend does, with the processor crash count before and after. Wait: the phone holds a wake lock on USB (devlab-usb-awake) and a phone that does not wake needs hands - prove one cycle by hand on surya first.  2026-11-17, from the deep-sleep research (docs decision 2026-11-17-deep-sleep-measured-s2idle; docs backlog sleep-measured-once is its first use): the cycle also reads the SoC's own counters before and after - /sys/kernel/debug/qcom_stats (cxsd, aosd, ddr, and adsp, cdsp, modem), suspend_stats, the cluster domain's idle states (pm_genpd power-domain-cluster) and every wakeup source's count - so one cycle says whether the SoC reached its floor and, if not, which processor stayed up and what woke it. On USB it can only work with the gadget let go for the length of the sleep (soft_connect) and the lab's and the shell's wake locks released; reach and read back over USB after the RTC wake. Once a cycle has run in a boot, the check soc-sleeps (base/90-sleep.sh) turns from skip to pass or fail in that boot's report.

title: The lab's ear
note: devlab hear and devlab health --hear work: a tone on each channel, recorded through the lab's microphone, measured against the silent room; heard checks join the one baseline when listened for. Its first results on surya were withdrawn - the microphone was being worn. It counts when the microphone has been placed by the phone, on notice.

title: devlab hear asks for the word first
note: devlab hear and devlab health --hear refuse without --placed, and say the procedure: tell the microphone's keeper, wait for their word. The lab's microphone can stay named: nothing plays by accident.

title: The microphone, placed on notice
note: The microphone can be relied on when it is placed by the phone. Before any listening test the agent notifies its keeper and waits for his word; only then is the test run, with --placed, and counted. The tool refuses otherwise.

title: The phone's own microphone, heard the same way
note: The lab plays a tone, the phone records it: the instrument for the long-open microphone work. And a second lab microphone, to tell left from right.

title: Listening by itself, at decent hours
note: The watcher stays silent: a tone after every start could sound at night. For it to listen unasked the lab needs to say when sound is welcome.

title: A room of exact zero means the microphone did not record
note: Right after a reboot the room recorded at -240 dBFS (digital silence) and the tones still passed. devlab hear should refuse in that case.

title: Safe test kernels
note: devlab kernel: one try by boot counting, a timeout that falls back to stock.

title: Never read LPASS pins through debugfs while LPASS is idle
note: Found by the bring-up session, 2026-11-17: reading /sys/kernel/debug/gpio and the LPASS LPI pinctrl debugfs on surya while the LPASS clocks were off stalled the bus; the phone hung until a person held power. A guard for agents: devlab phone root (and the MCP door) could refuse or warn on those paths, or the health suite never touch them. Recorded in surya-lab research/microphone.md.  2026-11-17 (orchestration): devlab now refuses, saying why, any command it carries to the phone (phone sh|root, the MCP door) that names a path in the manifest [[hazard]] list; the hand-written ssh it might go around is refused by the lab hooks (devlab guard). Next: surya-lab device.toml names its hazards (bring-up: /sys/kernel/debug/gpio and the LPI pinctrl debugfs under 62b40000), then the item is done.

title: Half-manual tests
note: Sequential tests with an observer - a person now, a rig later.

title: Reaches the phone
note: devlab phone: USB or Wi-Fi, no quoting layer, boot ids.

title: Built on postmarketOS's conventions
note: device.toml from deviceinfo; tests in the shape of pmOS's initramfs CI; bootrr.

title: Provisioning
note: Packages, files by {compatible}, Wi-Fi; the shared connection undone by a guard. It sets a fresh phone's clock and grows its system to fill its partition first.

title: A proper rig
note: Asked for by the author, for the future: a microphone fixed in place, a webcam that sees the screen, servos that press the buttons and touch the glass - so the tests that need a hand, an eye or an ear can run by themselves, for any phone.

title: suite put: find the runner by itself
note: Asked by the bring-up session, 2026-11-17: devlab suite put now requires --runner target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/devlab-health; a device lab's session has to know lab-tools' build path. Default it to the built runner (or build it), so putting a new check is one word.

title: kernel try: a try whose release equals the test kernel's is read as stock
note: Asked by the bring-up session, 2026-11-17. Five times that night devlab kernel try said 'pmos-wcdswr was chosen and stopped before it could log anything - is it an EFI image? stock 7.1.0-rc3-sm7150-wcd came back', while uname showed the phone running the try kernel (7.1.0-rc3-sm7150-wcd, its cmdline with initrd=initramfs-wcdswr). The try came, ran its health and stayed; devlab took it for stock. Then kernel install refused ('7.1.0-rc3-sm7150-wcd is the running kernel's version'), so each new try needed a devlab phone reboot first. Wanted: decide which entry booted by the running cmdline (initrd=initramfs-NAME) rather than the log file; and say plainly that the phone stays on the try until the next reboot - or reboot back to stock at the end of try, so the reference is stock again.

title: kernel try reports what came back
note: devlab kernel try reports what the try came to, said by the phone after a new boot answers: booted, not chosen, stopped early, or timed out with its log. Proven 2026-11-11: booted the microphone kernel in 81 s.
